Nuclear NDT training in Newport News: the short answer

Nuclear NDT training for Newport News employers and technicians is delivered by Atlantis NDT online, as live virtual classes, or onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight. The courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and build the method foundation (UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET) that naval-nuclear and commercial nuclear programmes then qualify on top of. Atlantis has no training centre in Newport News; quotes are on request and returned within one business day.

That last sentence matters for this city more than most. Newport News is not a place where a technician walks into a class, pays, and walks out "nuclear certified". Nuclear qualification here is layered. The bottom layer is method knowledge and employer certification under a written practice. On top of that sit the requirements of whoever owns the work: Naval Reactors and NAVSEA for the reactor plants built and refuelled at the shipyard, the utility and ASME Section XI for commercial plants such as Surry across the James River, and EPRI performance demonstration for certain ultrasonic examinations. This section explains each layer honestly, shows which parts our training covers, and where you will need your employer's programme to finish the job.

If you want to start the conversation now, request a nuclear NDT training quote for Newport News and tell us the methods, levels and head-count.

Nuclear NDT work in Newport News and the Virginia Peninsula

The general Newport News training page covers the city's whole NDT market. This page is narrower: it is about the examinations that touch a reactor plant, a reactor coolant boundary, or the nuclear supply chain that feeds them. In and around Newport News that work comes from four directions.

1. Naval-nuclear construction and refuelling at the shipyard

Newport News Shipbuilding, a division of HII, is the only US yard that builds nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and one of two that build nuclear submarines. It also performs refuelling and complex overhaul (RCOH) of carriers mid-way through their service life, and carrier inactivation at end of life. All three activities generate nuclear-scope examinations: welds on reactor plant piping and components, surface examinations on pressure-boundary parts, volumetric examination of welds that will never be accessible again once the plant is closed up, and an evidence trail that has to survive decades. The naval nuclear propulsion programme is run jointly by the Navy and the Department of Energy (Naval Reactors), not by the NRC, and its technical requirements reach the yard through NAVSEA documents and contract specifications.

2. Commercial nuclear power on the James River and beyond

Dominion Energy's Surry Power Station sits across the James River from Newport News, and North Anna operates in Louisa County. Both are NRC-licensed commercial reactors, inspected by NRC Region II, and their in-service inspection (ISI) programmes are written to ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section XI. Refuelling outages bring a surge of ISI scope: piping weld UT, vessel and nozzle examinations, steam generator eddy current, visual examinations of supports and internals, and surface examinations of welds and bolting. Much of that scope is performed by outage contractors who mobilise technicians from across the country, which is how many Peninsula technicians first see nuclear work.

3. The Virginia nuclear supply chain

Virginia hosts an unusual concentration of nuclear manufacturers and engineering firms. Lynchburg, a few hours west, is home to BWX Technologies' naval reactor component work and to Framatome's US engineering operations. Component manufacture for nuclear service brings ASME Section III fabrication examinations (RT, UT, MT, PT and VT of welds and materials), and suppliers to the naval programme work to the same NAVSEA requirements as the yard. Smaller machine shops and fabricators on the Peninsula and in Hampton Roads supply valves, piping spools, foundations and fittings into that chain, and each needs certified examiners on its own written practice.

4. Inspection and engineering service companies

Hampton Roads has a deep bench of inspection service companies and engineering contractors that support the shipyards, the naval station, the commercial plants and the DOE complex. Their technicians move between scopes, and a company that sends staff to a nuclear site needs a written practice that holds up to the customer's audit, technicians with documented training and experience, and a Level III who can sign for it.

Atlantis supports this market by training technicians in the methods, helping employers build or tighten their written practice, and providing Level III services. We do not train or certify to Naval Reactors, NAVSEA or EPRI PDI requirements directly; those qualifications are granted by the employer or the programme that owns them. See the full NDT training in Newport News page for the city-wide picture and the national nuclear NDT training page for how nuclear qualification works across the US.

Methods used on nuclear scope in Newport News

The table maps each method we train to the nuclear work it supports locally and to the code or standard that usually governs it. Code references are context: the governing document for any job is whatever the contract and the owner's programme specify.

MethodNuclear application around Newport NewsCode / standard usually invoked
UT (conventional)Reactor plant piping welds, component welds, thickness and lamination checks, ISI piping examinations at commercial plantsNAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 (naval); ASME Section XI and Section V (commercial)
PAUTEncoded weld examinations where a permanent, re-analysable record is wanted; dissimilar metal and austenitic welds on commercial ISI scopeASME Section V Article 4; ASME XI Appendix VIII where performance demonstration applies
TOFDFlaw sizing support on thick-section welds; usually paired with PAUT in encoded techniquesASME Section V; project specification
RTNew-construction welds on reactor plant and nuclear-grade piping where a film or digital image is the record of acceptanceNAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 and MIL-STD-2035 (naval); ASME Section III / V (commercial)
MTSurface examination of ferritic welds, forgings and boltingNAVSEA 271 / MIL-STD-2035; ASME Section V Article 7
PTSurface examination of austenitic stainless and nickel-alloy welds, with consumables controlled for halogens and sulphurNAVSEA 271 / MIL-STD-2035; ASME Section V Article 6
VTWeld visual inspection, ISI VT-1 / VT-2 / VT-3 categories on commercial plants, fit-up and final visual on naval workASME Section XI IWA-2210; NAVSEA 271
ETSteam generator and heat exchanger tubing at commercial plants; surface ET on componentsASME Section V Article 8; EPRI steam generator guidelines (utility programmes)

A local method spotlight: for nuclear work, the method most worth deep investment is ultrasonic testing. It carries most volumetric examination in service, it is the method where performance demonstration applies at commercial plants, and on new naval construction it increasingly sits alongside or replaces radiography where the specification allows. A technician with strong UT Level II fundamentals, followed by PAUT, is the most useful person on almost any nuclear crew. Our UT Level II course and phased array training are the usual starting points.

Which certification scheme Newport News nuclear employers expect

This is where honesty saves people time and money. Different owners require different schemes, and training is only one input into each. Here is how the main schemes relate to Atlantis's SNT-TC-1A-based training.

SchemeWho requires itDoes SNT-TC-1A training fit?
ASNT SNT-TC-1AMost fabricators, inspection companies and supply-chain shops; the base reference for many employer written practicesYes. This is what Atlantis trains to. The employer certifies under its written practice.
NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271Naval shipbuilding and repair, including reactor plant work at the yard and naval-programme suppliersPartly. Classroom training in the method is a foundation, but 271 has its own qualification and examination requirements administered under the employer's NAVSEA-compliant programme. Our training does not grant 271 qualification.
ANSI/ASNT CP-189Utilities and ISI vendors working to ASME Section XI, which references CP-189 for personnel qualificationPartly. CP-189 is a standard rather than a recommended practice and is stricter than SNT-TC-1A in places. Method training is relevant; the employer must still qualify you under its CP-189 programme.
EPRI PDI (ASME XI Appendix VIII)UT examiners on specific commercial ISI scopes (piping welds, vessel welds, bolting)No, not directly. PDI is a blind performance demonstration on flawed specimens. SNT-TC-1A training builds the UT knowledge you need to attempt it; it is not a substitute.
10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality programmeCommercial nuclear licensees and their safety-related suppliersContext. Appendix B governs the supplier's quality system, including how training and certification records are controlled. It shapes the written practice rather than replacing it.
ISO 9712 / ACCPSome international owners and a few US employersNo. Atlantis does not train to ISO 9712 or ACCP. Mentioned here only because some job postings list them.

The practical consequence: a Newport News technician who wants nuclear work should first hold solid SNT-TC-1A certifications from an employer, then join an employer whose programme qualifies people for nuclear scope. A company that wants to put people on nuclear scope should make sure its written practice, records and Level III arrangements will survive the customer's audit before it bids. We help with both.

The SNT-TC-1A path, step by step, for a Newport News nuclear technician

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. Under SNT-TC-1A, certification is employer-based. The written practice defines training hours, experience, exams and recertification for each method and level. If you are moving toward nuclear work, ask whether the written practice also references CP-189 or the NAVSEA requirements the company works to.
  2. Complete formal classroom training in each method. Hours are set by the written practice using SNT-TC-1A as the reference; our training requirements matrix lists the recommended minimums so you do not have to rely on memory or forum posts.
  3. Accumulate documented on-the-job experience in the method, under supervision of certified personnel. Nuclear employers look hard at experience records, so keep yours specific: component types, materials, techniques, and who supervised.
  4. Pass the general, specific and practical exams, administered under a Level III. The practical must be on real specimens with the equipment and procedures you will use.
  5. Pass the vision examination (near vision annually, colour contrast as the written practice requires).
  6. Be certified in writing by your employer. Certification is not portable between employers in the way a licence is; a new employer re-certifies under its own practice.
  7. Add the nuclear overlays: site-specific training, CP-189 qualification, PDI demonstration for applicable UT scopes, or the NAVSEA qualification your yard programme requires.
  8. Maintain and recertify on the interval the written practice sets, keeping vision tests current and records complete.

More detail on the scheme itself is on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page, and the level structure is explained on the Level II path.

Radiation licensing and site access around Newport News

Radiographic testing brings licensing requirements that sit outside SNT-TC-1A. Virginia became an NRC Agreement State in 2009, so industrial radiography using radioactive sources at commercial sites in Virginia is licensed by the Virginia Department of Health's Radioactive Materials Program rather than by the NRC directly. Radiographers working with sources must meet the state's radiographer requirements, which mirror the federal industrial radiography rules, including an independent radiographer certification and radiation safety training.

Two wrinkles matter for nuclear work on the Peninsula. First, commercial reactor sites are NRC-licensed facilities, and the radiography contractor works within both its own materials licence and the plant's radiation protection programme. Second, federal installations where the government holds exclusive jurisdiction fall back under NRC authority, so an Agreement State licensee may need NRC reciprocity before working there. The shipyard's own reactor plant radiological controls are a separate regime again, administered under the naval nuclear programme. Your employer's radiation safety officer is the person who confirms which applies to a given job; treat any training course, including ours, as preparation for that, not a licence.

Access is the other gate. Naval-nuclear work requires security clearance or vetting set by the yard and the government, US citizenship for many roles, and site-specific training. Commercial plants require unescorted-access authorisation through the licensee's access programme, including background checks and fitness-for-duty testing. None of that is part of method certification, and none of it can be shortcut by training, so plan for the lead time.

How Atlantis delivers nuclear-focused NDT training to Newport News crews

Atlantis does not run a classroom in Newport News, and we will not pretend to. Training is delivered three ways:

  • Live online: instructor-led classes for the theory and specific-exam preparation portions, suitable for individuals and for crews spread across the Peninsula, Norfolk and Lynchburg. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility: an ASNT Level III-led cohort at your shop or office, using your equipment, your procedures and your written practice. This is the strongest model for nuclear suppliers, because the practical exam and the training records end up exactly where the auditor expects them.
  • Blended: theory online, practical sessions and exams onsite, scheduled around outages, sea trials and RCOH milestones rather than a fixed public calendar.

Nuclear-specific emphasis we build into cohorts on request: cleanliness and consumable control for PT and MT on austenitic material, record discipline and traceability, procedure adherence when a procedure is more restrictive than the code, and how to read the acceptance criteria in NAVSEA 271 and MIL-STD-2035 versus ASME Section XI. If your crew needs that emphasis, ask about onsite nuclear NDT training for your Newport News crew.

Larger employer programmes are handled through corporate NDT training, which covers scheduling across sites and multiple methods.

Employer services: written practices and Level III support for Newport News nuclear suppliers

Most nuclear audit findings against small and mid-sized NDT employers are not about technique. They are about paper: a written practice that does not say what the company actually does, training hours that cannot be traced to a syllabus, experience logs with no supervisor named, an exam with no record of who graded it, or a Level III whose relationship to the company is undefined. Those findings stop a supplier being approved, or put an approved supplier on hold.

Atlantis helps with:

  • Written practice development and review against SNT-TC-1A, with notes on where a nuclear or naval customer will expect CP-189 or NAVSEA provisions. See NDT written practice development.
  • Level III services: exam preparation and administration, procedure review, technique sheets, and records audits before your customer does one.
  • Gap reviews for companies moving from general fabrication into nuclear supply, including how training and certification records should be controlled under an Appendix B quality programme.

For broader engineering support in the area, see NDT consulting in Newport News and nuclear NDT consulting in Norfolk. To get a reviewer looking at your documents, book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 methods in five 3D environments, including a lab, a welding workshop and an oil and gas site. For a nuclear-bound technician it is useful for drilling scan coverage, probe handling logic, indication recognition and the sequence of a procedure before time on real equipment. It is practice only: it does not replace hands-on training, and the practical exam must be taken on real specimens. A local entry point is the Practical NDT Newport News page.

Local options compared

People searching "nuclear NDT training Newport News" usually want a list. Here is an honest one.

  • The Apprentice School at Newport News Shipbuilding runs a multi-year, paid apprenticeship with a Non-Destructive Tester trade covering RT, MT, PT, UT, ET and VT plus codes and quality standards. If you want to work at the yard and can commit to an apprenticeship, it is the most direct route into naval-nuclear NDT. It is an employer pipeline, not an open course.
  • Virginia community colleges: Brightpoint Community College (formerly John Tyler) has long offered NDT coursework within its engineering technology programmes. Peninsula and Tidewater colleges are strong in welding, which is a common feeder into NDT. Check current catalogues before enrolling.
  • National training providers run scheduled public courses at their own centres or online and advertise Virginia city pages. They suit individuals who want a public class date.
  • Outage and ISI contractors train and qualify their own people for nuclear scope, including CP-189 and PDI. Joining one after gaining general certifications is the usual route into commercial nuclear.
  • Atlantis NDT fits employers and crews: live-online and onsite SNT-TC-1A training, written practice and Level III services, delivered to your schedule. We are not the right choice if you need NAVSEA 271 qualification issued by a third party or a PDI demonstration; nobody outside the owning programme can grant those.

For the statewide view, including other Virginia cities, see NDT training in Virginia.

Your instructor

Atlantis training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Cohorts are run under his Level III oversight, including exam administration where the employer's written practice designates Atlantis as the outside agency.

Frequently asked questions about nuclear NDT training in Newport News

Where can I get nuclear NDT training in Newport News?

There is no single "nuclear NDT course" that qualifies you for nuclear work. You build method certifications under SNT-TC-1A first, through an employer, a college programme or a provider such as Atlantis (online or onsite), and then the nuclear employer qualifies you to its programme. The shipyard's Apprentice School is the main route into naval-nuclear work at the yard itself.

Does Atlantis NDT training qualify me for work at Newport News Shipbuilding?

It builds the method knowledge, but naval-nuclear examinations at the yard require qualification under NAVSEA requirements administered within the yard's or contractor's programme. No outside course grants that on its own.

What is the difference between SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 for nuclear work?

SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice that each employer adapts in its written practice. ANSI/ASNT CP-189 is a standard with firmer minimum requirements and is referenced by ASME Section XI for in-service inspection personnel. Many utilities and ISI vendors require CP-189. SNT-TC-1A training is relevant preparation, but the employer still qualifies you under CP-189.

Can I take nuclear NDT training online in Virginia?

Theory and exam preparation, yes. Atlantis runs live online classes for Virginia technicians. Practical training and the practical exam must be hands-on with real equipment and specimens, which we deliver onsite at the employer's facility.

What is EPRI PDI and do I need it?

The EPRI Performance Demonstration Initiative qualifies UT examiners and procedures for specific ASME Section XI Appendix VIII scopes by blind testing on flawed specimens. You need it only for those scopes, usually through an ISI vendor. Strong UT Level II skills are the prerequisite; no classroom course replaces the demonstration.

Which NDT method is most in demand for nuclear work?

Ultrasonic testing, including phased array, carries most volumetric in-service examination and is where performance demonstration applies. Eddy current is the specialist method for steam generator tubing. Surface methods and visual examination are needed on almost every scope.

Do I need a licence to do radiography in Virginia?

Your employer needs a radioactive materials licence from the Virginia Department of Health (Virginia is an NRC Agreement State), and you must meet the state's radiographer training and certification requirements. Work on exclusive-federal-jurisdiction sites can require NRC reciprocity. NDT method certification is separate from these radiation safety requirements.

How long does it take to become a nuclear NDT technician?

It depends on the methods, the levels and the employer's written practice, because classroom hours and experience are cumulative per method. Our training requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums; nuclear qualification then adds employer- and site-specific steps.

What does nuclear NDT training cost in Newport News?

Atlantis quotes on request. The price depends on methods and levels, group size, whether delivery is online or onsite, and whether you need written practice or Level III support alongside the training. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding for NDT training?

Those programmes generally require an approved school or an eligible training provider listed for your area. Atlantis does not claim that approval; check the provider lists before you plan on public funding. Many nuclear-bound technicians are trained at employer expense instead.

Are naval nuclear veterans a good fit for NDT?

Often, yes. Veterans from nuclear ratings bring procedure discipline and radiological-controls experience, and can clear access requirements faster. They still need method certification under an employer's written practice. See veterans transitioning into NDT.

Is this page different from the maritime NDT training page for Newport News?

Yes. This page covers nuclear scope: reactor plant work, commercial nuclear ISI and the nuclear supply chain. The maritime NDT training in Newport News page covers hull and structural examination, class and NAVSEA structural requirements and shipyard production work.
